Visual and ephemeral surfaces

Screens 16–18. Science generates outstanding visual material that currently goes to Instagram instead. Three surfaces reclaim it, each carrying its workbook mitigation as a hard constraint: an image cannot post without linked data, a story is explicitly outside the citable record, and a video demo cannot exist without its written protocol.

THE TWO RULES THIS FEED ENFORCES
01Underlying data must be linked. A figure with no attached data cannot be posted here at all. The mitigation for aesthetic selection bias is to make the beautiful image inseparable from the numbers behind it.
02Integrity screening runs on upload. Duplicate-region and splice detection, the same checks as the manuscript integrity screen. Findings are advisory and go to the poster first, never public.
AND WHAT IS ABSENT
No filters. No colour presets. No "enhance". The upload path offers exactly one adjustment — a linear brightness match — and records it in the metadata where a reader can see it.
An image tool that makes a gel look better is an image tool for committing misconduct. There is no such control anywhere in this product.

WHY EPHEMERAL CONTENT EXISTS IN A RECORD-KEEPING PRODUCT
The workbook is blunt that ephemerality is philosophically at odds with the scientific record. It is here anyway, for one reason: the low stakes unlock posting by people who would never write a post. A PhD student will photograph a plate at midnight; the same student will not write a lab update.
THE FOUR CONSTRAINTS THAT MAKE IT SAFE
The orange banner is permanent chrome, in the composer and the viewer.
Lab visibility maximum. A story can never be Public.
Not searchable, not in the feed, not in the audit trail, no DOI possible.
No view counts, no "who saw this", no reply-to-story inbox.
MAKE PERMANENT · THE ESCAPE HATCH
If the plate photograph turns out to matter, one action promotes it into a real artifact: it becomes a figure with a caption, a visibility choice and a place in the project — and it stops expiring.
